However, if a condition is to be imposed or amended after a servicing licence is granted, the Secretary must invite the servicing licensee to make written submissions in relation to the proposed condition or amendment before imposing the condition, or making the amendment.
The invitation must:
be in writing; and
state the period of not less than 14 days within which the submission must be made.
Without limiting the generality of subsection (1), a condition may restrict to a specified class or classes the measuring instruments that may be verified under the servicing licence.
The Secretary must notify the servicing licensee in writing of:
the terms of any condition imposed on the servicing licence; and
the terms of any condition of the servicing licence as amended; and
the revocation of any condition of the servicing licence.
The amendment or revocation of a condition of the servicing licence takes effect on the later of:
the day on which the notice is given; or
the day specified in the notice.

section.heading: Conditions on all servicing licences

content.p: A servicing licence is subject to the following conditions:
if the servicing licensee is an individual—a condition that the servicing licensee must not personally verify a measuring instrument unless he or she is competent to do so;
a condition that the servicing licensee must not employ a person to verify a measuring instrument unless he or she is competent to do so;

a condition that the servicing licensee or an employee of the servicing licensee must not mark a measuring instrument with the servicing licensee’s mark without first obliterating any other verification mark that the instrument already bears;

a condition that any obliteration by the servicing licensee or an employee of the servicing licensee of a verification mark without verification of the measuring instrument must be reported in writing to the Secretary within 14 days or such shorter period as is specified in the licence;

a condition that if the servicing licensee or an employee of the servicing licensee determines, when examining or testing a measuring instrument, that the instrument could not be verified, the servicing licensee must report the fact in writing to the Secretary within 14 days or such shorter period as is specified in the licence unless a report of the matter is also required under paragraph (d);

a condition that the servicing licensee or an employee of the servicing licensee must not verify a measuring instrument without using such equipment as is specified by the Secretary when granting the licence;

a condition that if the servicing licensee’s mark is made by an employee of the servicing licensee, the servicing licensee must at all times be able from that mark to identify the employee to the Secretary;
a condition that the date on which the servicing licensee or an employee of the servicing licensee verifies a measuring instrument must be included with the servicing licensee’s mark;

a condition that the servicing licensee must provide such classes and denominations, as are determined by the Secretary, of reference standards of measurement as are necessary for the exercise of the powers or the performance of the functions of the servicing licensee;
such other conditions as may be prescribed.

section.heading: Application to amend a condition of a servicing licence

content.p: A servicing licensee may apply to the Secretary for an amendment of a condition of the servicing licence imposed under section 18NG.
The application:
must be in writing in the form approved by the Secretary; and
must be accompanied by the application fee prescribed for the purposes of this paragraph; and
must be accompanied by such other material as is prescribed.
The Secretary may:
grant the application; or
refuse the application.
The Secretary must give the servicing licensee written notice of the decision on the application within 28 days after the application is made.
If the Secretary fails to give the servicing licensee written notice of the decision within that period, the Secretary is, at the end of the period, taken to have refused to grant the application.

section.heading: Application to change servicing licensee due to change of partnership

content.p: This section applies if:
a partnership is a servicing licensee; and
(b) there is or is proposed to be a change to the membership of the partnership (the change) with at least one partner before the change continuing as a partner after the change.
The partnership may apply to the Secretary to amend the servicing licence to state the partners who are or will be the partners after the change.
The application:
must be in writing in the form approved by the Secretary; and
must include information about how the partnership has changed or is proposed to change; and
must include information about any new partner that the new partner would have to have given to the Secretary if the new partner were applying to be a servicing licensee; and
must be accompanied by the application fee prescribed for the purposes of this paragraph.
To the extent the change involves a person ceasing to be a partner, the Secretary must grant the application and amend the servicing licence to remove the name of the partner from the licence.
To the extent the change involves a new partner being admitted to the partnership, the Secretary must, after considering the application:
grant the application and amend the servicing licence to include the name of the new partner; or
refuse the application.
The Secretary must notify the partnership in writing of the decision.
The Secretary must refuse an application under subsection (2) if the Secretary would have had to refuse an application under section 18NC if the new partner were applying to be a servicing licensee.
From the day on which the amendment of the servicing licence takes effect, the licence is taken to be held by the partnership as it exists on that day.
The amendment of the servicing licence takes effect:
if the partnership changed more than 28 days before the application for amendment of the licence was made—at the start of that 28th day; or
if the partnership is changed on or after that 28th day but before the end of the day on which the application is decided—on the day on which the partnership was changed; or
if the partnership changes on a later day—on that later day.

section.heading: Application for renewal of servicing licence

content.p: A servicing licensee may apply to the Secretary for the renewal of the licensee’s servicing licence.
The application:
must be in the form approved by the Secretary; and
must be accompanied by the application fee prescribed for the purposes of this paragraph; and
must be accompanied by such other material as is prescribed.

The Secretary may, by notice in writing to an applicant, request the applicant to provide to the Secretary information or documents of the kind specified in the notice within a specified period of not less than 14 days.
The Secretary may refuse the application if the notice is not complied with.

section.heading: Renewal of servicing licence

content.p: The Secretary must grant an application for the renewal of a servicing licence unless:
the Secretary would have had to refuse the application under section 18NC if it had been an application made under section 18NA; or
the Secretary decides to refuse the application under subsection 18NK(4).

(2) The Secretary must give the applicant written notice of the decision on the application within 28 days after the application is made (the consideration period) and, if the renewal is granted, specify the period of the renewal in the notice.
The notice must specify the period for which the licence is renewed.

If the Secretary requests an applicant under subsection 18NK(3) to provide information or documents, the time taken by the applicant to provide the information or documents is not to be included in the consideration period.

If the Secretary fails to give the applicant written notice of the decision under subsection (2) within the consideration period the Secretary is, at the end of the period, taken to have refused to grant the application.

section.heading: Surrender and transfer of servicing licence

content.p: A servicing licensee may surrender the licence by notice in writing given to the Secretary.
Subject to section 18NJ, a servicing licence is not transferable.

section.heading: Order preventing employment of certain persons

content.p: The Secretary may, by order in writing, direct that a specified person:
is not to be employed by a servicing licensee to verify any measuring instrument; or
is not to be employed by a servicing licensee to verify a specified class or classes of measuring instruments; or
is to be employed by a servicing licensee to verify any measuring instrument, or verify a specified class or classes of measuring instrument, only in compliance with specified conditions.

The Secretary must not make such an order unless satisfied that it is necessary to do so because of the person’s lack of competency, or lack of fitness in any other respect, to exercise the functions concerned.
If the Secretary makes an order under this section, the Secretary must:
serve a copy of the order on the person to whom it relates (if the person’s whereabouts are known to the Secretary); and
serve a copy of the order on each servicing licensee that the Secretary knows is employing that person when the order is made.
The order comes into force on the last day on which it is served.
It is a condition of the servicing licence of that servicing licensee that the servicing licensee must not employ a person in contravention of an order in force under this section.

section.heading: Offence—breaching a condition of a servicing licence

content.p: A person commits an offence if:
the person is a servicing licensee; and
the person engages or fails to engage in conduct; and
the conduct or failure is in breach of a condition of the person’s servicing licence.
Penalty: 30 penalty units.
A person commits an offence if:
the person is a servicing licensee; and
an employee of the person engages or fails to engage in conduct; and
the conduct or failure is in breach of a condition of the person’s servicing licence; and
the person expressly, tacitly or impliedly authorises or permits the conduct or failure.
Penalty: 30 penalty units.
A person commits an offence if:
the person is an employee of a servicing licensee; and
the person engages or fails to engage in conduct; and
the conduct or failure is in breach of a condition of the servicing licensee’s servicing licence; and
the conduct or failure is not within the actual or apparent scope of the person’s employment.
Penalty: 30 penalty units.
Subsections (1), (2) and (3) are offences of strict liability.
Note: For strict liability, see section 6.1 of the Criminal Code.

section.heading: Overview

content.p: Overview of Part
Public weighbridge licences are granted by the Secretary on application.
The Secretary must refuse an application if the applicant does not meet certain suitability requirements.

There are conditions that are common to all public weighbridge licences. In addition, the Secretary may impose conditions on a public weighbridge licence. New conditions may be imposed, or existing conditions amended or revoked, during the life of the licence.
Public weighbridge licences are granted for a period, but may be renewed on application.

section.heading: Application for a public weighbridge licence

content.p: A person may make an application to the Secretary for a public weighbridge licence for a single weighbridge.
2 or more persons who carry on business together as partners may make an application jointly for a public weighbridge licence for a single weighbridge.
The application:
must be in the form approved by the Secretary; and
must be accompanied by the application fee prescribed for the purposes of this paragraph; and
must be accompanied by such other material as is prescribed.

The Secretary may, by notice in writing to an applicant, request the applicant to provide information or documents of the kind specified in the notice to the Secretary within a specified period of not less than 14 days.
The Secretary may refuse the application if the notice is not complied with.

section.heading: Granting a public weighbridge licence

content.p: The Secretary must grant an application for a public weighbridge licence for a single weighbridge unless there are grounds for refusal under this Act.
Note: The Secretary may refuse to grant a public weighbridge licence:
if the applicant fails to comply with a request for further information or documents (see subsection 18PA(4)); or
because of other circumstances set out in section 18PC.
(2) The Secretary must give the applicant written notice of the decision on the application within 28 days after the application is made (the consideration period).
The notice must specify the period for which the licence is granted.

If the Secretary requests an applicant under subsection 18PA(4) to provide information or documents, the time taken by the applicant to provide the information or documents is not to be included in the consideration period.

If the Secretary fails to give the applicant written notice of the decision under subsection (2) within the consideration period the Secretary is, at the end of the period, taken to have refused to grant the application.

section.heading: Circumstances in which public weighbridge licence must be refused

content.p: The Secretary must refuse an application by an applicant for a public weighbridge licence for a single weighbridge if:
the applicant is an individual who has not reached the age of 18 years; or
the applicant holds a licence under this Act that is suspended; or
the applicant is disqualified under this Act from holding a licence under this Act; or
neither:
the applicant; nor
an employee of the applicant; nor
a person who has contracted with the applicant to operate the weighbridge; nor
any employee of a person mentioned in subparagraph (iii);
is competent to operate a public weighbridge; or
the applicant or a person who has contracted with the applicant to operate the weighbridge is not likely to carry on the operation of a public weighbridge honestly and fairly; or
the applicant or a person who has contracted with the applicant to operate the weighbridge is in any other way not a fit and proper person to operate a public weighbridge; or
the Secretary considers that the weighbridge is not suitable for use as a public weighbridge.

(2) Without limiting the generality of paragraph (1)(f), the Secretary may have regard to any or all of the following matters in determining whether the applicant or a person who has contracted with the applicant to operate the weighbridge (the contractor) is a fit and proper person to operate a public weighbridge:

whether the applicant or the contractor has, during the period of 10 years that immediately preceded the making of the application, been convicted of, or served any part of a term of imprisonment for, an offence (whether under the law of the Commonwealth or any other law) involving fraud or dishonesty;
whether the applicant or the contractor was, when the application was made, the subject of a charge pending in relation to such an offence;
whether the applicant or the contractor has, at any time, been convicted of an offence against this Act or an earlier corresponding law;
whether the applicant or the contractor has been refused a licence under this Act or an earlier corresponding law.

section.heading: Where the applicant is a body corporate

content.p: If the applicant or the person who has contracted with the applicant to operate the weighbridge is a body corporate, paragraph 18PC(1)(f) and paragraphs 18PC(2)(a) to (d) apply as if a reference to the applicant or the person who has contracted with the applicant to operate the weighbridge included a reference to a person concerned in the management of the body corporate.

section.heading: Where the applicant is a partnership

content.p: If the applicant is a partnership, this Division applies as if:
a reference to the applicant, other than in subparagraph 18PC(1)(d)(i), were a reference to each member of the partnership; and
the reference to the applicant in subparagraph 18PC(1)(d)(i) were a reference to any partner in the partnership.
If the Secretary grants a public weighbridge licence to a partnership the licence must state:
the names of all the partners; and
if the partnership has a registered business name, the registered business name.
Each of the partners named on the public weighbridge licence is taken to be a public weighbridge licensee for the purposes of this Act.

section.heading: Register of public weighbridge licences

content.p: The Secretary must keep a register of prescribed particulars relating to public weighbridge licences.

section.heading: Conditions may be imposed on public weighbridge licences

content.p: The Secretary may impose conditions on a public weighbridge licence.
A condition may be imposed at the time the public weighbridge licence is granted or at a later time.
A condition may be amended or revoked at any time.

However, if a condition is to be imposed or amended after a public weighbridge licence is granted, the Secretary must invite the public weighbridge licensee to make written submissions in relation to the proposed condition or amendment before imposing the condition, or making the amendment.
The invitation must:
be in writing; and
state the period of not less than 14 days within which the submission must be made.
The Secretary must notify the public weighbridge licensee in writing of:
the terms of any condition imposed on the public weighbridge licence; and
the terms of any condition of the public weighbridge licence as amended; and
the revocation of any condition of the public weighbridge licence.
The amendment or revocation of a condition of the public weighbridge licence takes effect on the later of:
the day on which the notice is given; or
the day specified in the notice.

section.heading: Conditions on all public weighbridge licences

content.p: A public weighbridge licence is subject to the following conditions:
a condition that the weighbridge mentioned in the licence is to be located at the place stated in the licence;
a condition that the public weighbridge licensee must ensure that, if the weighbridge mentioned in the licence is made available as a public weighbridge, it is not operated by any person other than:
the public weighbridge licensee; or
an employee of the public weighbridge licensee; or
a person who has contracted with the public weighbridge licensee to operate the weighbridge; or
an employee of a person mentioned in subparagraph (iii);
if the public weighbridge licensee is an individual—a condition that the public weighbridge licensee must not personally operate the weighbridge mentioned in the licence unless competent to do so;
a condition that the public weighbridge licensee must not employ a person to operate the weighbridge mentioned in the licence unless the person is competent to do so;
a condition that the public weighbridge licensee must not contract with another person to operate the weighbridge mentioned in the licence unless:
where the contractor will operate the weighbridge personally—the contractor is competent to do so; and
where an employee of the contractor will operate the weighbridge—the employee is competent to do so;
such other conditions as may be prescribed.
The condition mentioned in paragraph (1)(b) does not apply to the operation of a weighbridge if:
the weighbridge is approved in writing by the Secretary for direct operation by the public; and
the public weighbridge licensee ensures that:
the weighbridge is not operated otherwise than in accordance with that condition; and
the weighbridge is operated only during such periods and in accordance with such conditions as specified in the approval.

section.heading: Application to amend a condition of a public weighbridge licence

content.p: A public weighbridge licensee may apply to the Secretary for an amendment of a condition of the licensee’s public weighbridge licence imposed under section 18PG.
The application:
must be in writing in the form approved by the Secretary; and
must be accompanied by the application fee prescribed for the purposes of this paragraph; and
must be accompanied by such other material as is prescribed.
The Secretary may:
grant the application; or
refuse the application.
The Secretary must give the public weighbridge licensee written notice of the decision on the application within 28 days after the application is made.

If the Secretary fails to give the public weighbridge licensee written notice of the decision within that period, the Secretary is, at the end of the period, taken to have refused to grant the application.

section.heading: Application to change public weighbridge licensee due to change of partnership

content.p: This section applies if:
a partnership is a public weighbridge licensee; and
(b) there is or is proposed to be a change to the membership of the partnership (the change) with at least one partner before the change continuing as a partner after the change.
The partnership may apply to the Secretary to amend the public weighbridge licence to state the partners who are or will be the partners after the change.
The application:
must be in writing in the form approved by the Secretary; and
must include information about how the partnership has changed or is proposed to change; and
must include information about any new partner that the new partner would have to have given to the Secretary if the new partner were applying to be a public weighbridge licensee; and
must be accompanied by the application fee prescribed for the purposes of this paragraph.

To the extent the change involves a person ceasing to be a partner, the Secretary must grant the application and amend the public weighbridge licence to remove the name of the partner from the licence.
To the extent the change involves a new partner being admitted to the partnership, the Secretary must, after considering the application:
grant the application and amend the public weighbridge licence to include the name of the new partner; or
refuse the application.
The Secretary must notify the partnership in writing of the decision.

The Secretary must refuse an application under subsection (2) if the Secretary would have had to refuse an application under section 18PC if the new partner were applying to be a public weighbridge licensee.
From the day on which the amendment of the public weighbridge licence takes effect, the licence is taken to be held by the partnership as it exists on that day.
The amendment of the public weighbridge licence takes effect:
if the partnership changed more than 28 days before the application for amendment of the licence was made—at the start of that 28th day; or
if the partnership is changed on or after that 28th day but before the end of the day on which the application is decided—on the day on which the partnership was changed; or
if the partnership changes on a later day—on that later day.

section.heading: Application to contract out the operation of the public weighbridge

content.p: This section applies if, during the term of a public weighbridge licence:
(a) the public weighbridge licensee enters into, or proposes to enter into, a contract with another person to operate the public weighbridge (the contractor); and
the public weighbridge licensee did not apply for the public weighbridge licence on the basis that the contractor would operate the public weighbridge.

The public weighbridge licensee may apply to the Secretary to amend the public weighbridge licence to state the person who will operate the public weighbridge after the contract or variation takes effect.
The application:
must be in writing in the form approved by the Secretary; and
must include a copy of the contract or proposed contract; and

must include any information about the contractor, or proposed contractor, that the public weighbridge licensee would have to have given to the Secretary if the licensee had applied for the public weighbridge licence on the basis that the contractor would operate the public weighbridge; and
must be accompanied by the application fee prescribed for the purposes of this paragraph.
The Secretary must, after considering the application:
grant the application and amend the public weighbridge licence to include the name of the contractor; or
refuse the application.
The Secretary must notify the public weighbridge licensee in writing of the decision.

The Secretary must refuse an application under subsection (2) if the Secretary would have had to refuse an application under section 18PC if the public weighbridge licensee were applying for a public weighbridge licence on the basis that the contractor would operate the public weighbridge.

section.heading: Application for renewal of public weighbridge licence

content.p: A public weighbridge licensee may apply to the Secretary for the renewal of the licensee’s public weighbridge licence.
The application:
must be in the form approved by the Secretary; and
must be accompanied by the application fee prescribed for the purposes of this paragraph; and
must be accompanied by such other material as is prescribed.

The Secretary may, by notice in writing to an applicant, request the applicant to provide to the Secretary information or documents of the kind specified in the notice within a specified period of not less than 14 days.
The Secretary may refuse the application if the notice is not complied with.

section.heading: Renewal of public weighbridge licence

content.p: The Secretary must grant an application for the renewal of a public weighbridge licence unless:
the Secretary would have had to refuse the application under section 18PC if it had been an application made under section 18PA; or
the Secretary decides to refuse the application under subsection 18PL(4).

(2) The Secretary must give the applicant written notice of the decision on the application within 28 days after the application is made (the consideration period) and, if the renewal is granted, specify the period of the renewal in the notice.
The notice must specify the period for which the licence is granted.

If the Secretary requests an applicant under subsection 18PL(3) to provide information or documents, the time taken by the applicant to provide the information or documents is not to be included in the consideration period.

If the Secretary fails to give the applicant written notice of the decision under subsection (2) within the consideration period the Secretary is, at the end of the period, taken to have refused to grant the application.

section.heading: Surrender and transfer of public weighbridge licence

content.p: A public weighbridge licensee may surrender the licence by notice in writing given to the Secretary.
Subject to section 18PJ, a public weighbridge licence is not transferable.

section.heading: Effect of relocation of licensed public weighbridge

content.p: (1) This section applies if a public weighbridge licensee moves a weighbridge from the location at which it was inspected before it was licensed to another location at the place stated in the licence.
The public weighbridge licence for the weighbridge is taken to have been surrendered under section 18PN.

section.heading: If weighbridge no longer suitable for use as public weighbridge

content.p: This section applies if the Secretary decides a licensed public weighbridge is no longer suitable for use as a public weighbridge.
The Secretary may give the public weighbridge licensee for the weighbridge a notice stating:
why the Secretary considers the weighbridge is no longer suitable for use as a public weighbridge; and
that the licensee may make a written submission to the Secretary within 28 days stating why the licensee considers the public weighbridge licence should not be revoked.
After considering any submissions made to the Secretary within the relevant period, the Secretary may:
decide to take no further action against the public weighbridge licensee; or
revoke the public weighbridge licence.
The Secretary must give the public weighbridge licensee written notice of the Secretary’s decision under subsection (3) within 14 days after making the decision.

section.heading: Order preventing employment of certain persons

content.p: The Secretary may, by order in writing, direct that a specified person:
is not to be employed by a public weighbridge licensee to perform duties relating to the operation of any public weighbridge; or
is to be employed by a public weighbridge licensee to perform duties relating to the operation of any public weighbridge only in compliance with specified conditions.

The Secretary must not make such an order unless satisfied that it is necessary to do so because of the person’s lack of competency, or lack of fitness in any other respect, to exercise the functions concerned.
If the Secretary makes an order under this section, the Secretary must:
serve a copy of the order on the person to whom it relates (if the person’s whereabouts are known to the Secretary); and
serve a copy of the order on each public weighbridge licensee that the Secretary knows is employing that person when the order is made.
The order comes into force on the last day on which it is served.
It is a condition of each public weighbridge licence of that public weighbridge licensee that the licensee must not employ a person in contravention of an order in force under this section.

section.heading: Order preventing contract with certain person to operate public weighbridge

content.p: The Secretary may, by order in writing, direct that:
a public weighbridge licensee must terminate any contract with a specified person to operate any public weighbridge; or
a public weighbridge licensee is to continue to contract with a specified person to operate any public weighbridge only in compliance with specified conditions.

The Secretary must not make such an order unless satisfied that it is necessary to do so because of the person’s lack of competency, or lack of fitness in any other respect, to exercise the functions concerned.
If the Secretary makes an order under this section, the Secretary must:
serve a copy of the order on the person to whom it relates (if the person’s whereabouts are known to the Secretary); and
serve a copy of the order on each public weighbridge licensee that the Secretary knows has contracted with the person when the order is made.
The order comes into force on the last day on which it is served.
It is a condition of each public weighbridge licence of that public weighbridge licensee that the licensee must comply with an order in force under this section.

It is a condition of each contract entered into by the public weighbridge licensee, either before or after the public weighbridge licence is granted, that the licensee may vary or terminate the contract if required to do so to comply with an order in force under this section.

section.heading: Order preventing employee of a public weighbridge contractor from operating public weighbridge

content.p: The Secretary may, by order in writing, direct that a specified person:

(a) is not to be employed by a person who has contracted with a public weighbridge licensee to operate a public weighbridge (a contractor) to perform duties relating to the operation of any public weighbridge; or
is to be employed by a contractor to perform duties relating to the operation of any public weighbridge only in compliance with specified conditions.

The Secretary must not make such an order unless satisfied that it is necessary to do so because of the person’s lack of competency, or lack of fitness in any other respect, to exercise the functions concerned.
If the Secretary makes an order under this section, the Secretary must:
serve a copy of the order on the person to whom it relates (if the person’s whereabouts are known to the Secretary); and
serve a copy of the order on each contractor that the Secretary knows employs the person when the order is made; and
serve a copy of the order on each public weighbridge licensee who the Secretary knows has contracted with each such contractor to operate a public weighbridge.
The order comes into force on the last day on which it is served.

It is a condition of each public weighbridge licence of each of those public weighbridge licensees that the licensee must terminate a contract for the operation of a public weighbridge with any contractor who employs the person in contravention of an order in force under this section.

It is a condition of each contract for the operation of a public weighbridge entered into by a public weighbridge licensee, either before or after the public weighbridge licence is granted, that the licensee may terminate the contract if required to do so to comply with subsection (4).

division.heading: Offences in relation to public weighbridges

section.heading: Offence—making a weighbridge available as a public weighbridge when not licensed etc.

content.p: A person commits an offence if:
the person makes a weighbridge available as a public weighbridge; and
the person is not:
a public weighbridge licensee; or
an employee of a public weighbridge licensee; or
a person who has contracted with a public weighbridge licensee to operate the weighbridge as a public weighbridge; or
an employee of a person mentioned in subparagraph (iii).
Penalty: 30 penalty units.
Subsection (1) is an offence of strict liability.
Note: For strict liability, see section 6.1 of the Criminal Code.

section.heading: Offence—breaching a condition of a public weighbridge licence

content.p: Public weighbridge licensee
A person commits an offence if:
the person is a public weighbridge licensee; and
the person engages or fails to engage in conduct; and
the conduct or failure is in breach of a condition of the person’s public weighbridge licence.
Penalty: 30 penalty units.
A person commits an offence if:
the person is a public weighbridge licensee; and
an employee of the person engages or fails to engage in conduct; and
the conduct or failure is in breach of a condition of the person’s public weighbridge licence; and
the person expressly, tacitly or impliedly authorises or permits the conduct or failure.
Penalty: 30 penalty units.
Employee of public weighbridge licensee
A person commits an offence if:
the person is an employee of a public weighbridge licensee; and
the person engages or fails to engage in conduct; and
that conduct or failure is in breach of a condition of the public weighbridge licensee’s licence; and
the conduct or failure is not within the actual or apparent scope of the person’s employment.
Penalty: 30 penalty units.
Person who contracts with public weighbridge licensee to operate weighbridge
A person commits an offence if:
the person contracts with a public weighbridge licensee to operate a public weighbridge; and
the person engages or fails to engage in conduct; and
the conduct or failure is in breach of a condition of the public weighbridge licensee’s licence.
Penalty: 30 penalty units.
A person commits an offence if:
the person contracts with a public weighbridge licensee to operate a public weighbridge; and
an employee of the person engages or fails to engage in conduct; and
the conduct or failure is in breach of a condition of the public weighbridge licensee’s licence; and
the person expressly, tacitly or impliedly authorises or permits the conduct or failure.
Penalty: 30 penalty units.
Employee of person who contracts with public weighbridge licensee to operate weighbridge
A person commits an offence if:
the person is an employee of a person who contracts with a public weighbridge licensee to operate a public weighbridge; and
the person engages or fails to engage in conduct; and
that conduct or failure is in breach of a condition of the public weighbridge licensee’s licence; and
the conduct or failure is not within the actual or apparent scope of the person’s employment.
Penalty: 30 penalty units.
Subsections (1) to (6) are offences of strict liability.
Note: For strict liability, see section 6.1 of the Criminal Code.

part.heading: Disciplinary action against servicing licensees and public weighbridge licensees

section.heading: Overview

content.p: Overview of Part
This Part contains provisions about the disciplinary action that may be taken against servicing licensees and public weighbridge licensees.
Section 18QA sets out the grounds on which disciplinary action may be taken.
The kinds of disciplinary action that may be taken are:
reprimanding the licensee; or
imposing a condition on the licence; or
suspending the licence; or
cancelling the licence; or
accepting an enforceable undertaking from the licensee; or
publicising information about particular disciplinary action.

section.heading: Grounds for disciplinary action

content.p: Each of the following constitutes grounds for disciplinary action against a servicing licensee or a public weighbridge licensee:
the licensee has failed to comply with a provision of this Act, or with a condition of the licence;
the licensee has been found guilty of an offence involving fraud or dishonesty;

in the case of a servicing licensee—continuously, for a period prescribed by the regulations, neither the licensee nor any employee of the licensee is competent to perform the functions and duties of a verifier;
in the case of a public weighbridge licensee—continuously, for a period prescribed by the regulations, neither:
the licensee; nor
an employee of the licensee; nor
a person who contracts with the licensee to operate the weighbridge; nor
an employee of a person mentioned in subparagraph (iii);
has the competencies appropriate to operate the public weighbridge;
the activities to which the licence relates are being carried on in a dishonest or unfair manner;
the Secretary would be required by sections 18NC or 18PC to refuse an application for a licence by the licensee (if the licensee were not already licensed);
the licensee has been refused a licence under this Act or an earlier corresponding law;
the licensee is the subject of disciplinary action under section 18QC or under the equivalent provision of an earlier corresponding law;
the licensee is not, for any other reason, a fit and proper person to continue to hold a licence.
A ground for disciplinary action under subsection (1) exists in relation to a licensee that is a partnership if:
in relation to the grounds mentioned in paragraphs (a), (b), (f), (g), (h) and (i)—the ground exists in relation to any one or more of the members of the partnership; and
in relation to the grounds mentioned in paragraphs (c) and (d)—neither the partners nor anyone else mentioned in those paragraphs has the competencies mentioned in those paragraphs.

A ground for disciplinary action under paragraph (1)(i) exists in relation to a licensee that is a body corporate if it exists in relation to a person concerned in the management of the body corporate.

section.heading: Notice to licensee of grounds for disciplinary action

content.p: If the Secretary reasonably suspects that there are grounds for disciplinary action against a servicing licensee or a public weighbridge licensee, the Secretary may serve a written notice on the licensee:
giving full particulars of those grounds, including particulars for the reasons for any general ground; and

calling on the licensee to show cause within a reasonable period specified in the notice why the Secretary should not take disciplinary action on those grounds against the licensee under section 18QC.
A licensee on whom such a notice is served may, within the period allowed by the notice, make a written submission to the Secretary on the matters concerned.

section.heading: Taking disciplinary action

content.p: If, after consideration of any submissions made by the licensee within the period allowed, the Secretary is satisfied that grounds for disciplinary action against a licensee have been established, the Secretary may:
reprimand the licensee; or
impose a condition on the licence; or
suspend the licence for up to 12 months; or
act under any combination of 2 or more of paragraphs (a), (b) and (c); or
cancel the licence and disqualify the former licensee permanently or for a specified period from holding a licence.
The Secretary may take the disciplinary action by written notice given to the licensee.
That notice takes effect:
at the end of the period for lodging an application for a review of the decision by the Administrative Review Tribunal; and
if such an application has been made within that period—when the application is withdrawn or finally determined, unless the Administrative Review Tribunal orders otherwise.

section.heading: Accepting undertakings

content.p: The Secretary may, either instead of or in addition to taking disciplinary action under section 18QC, accept a written undertaking given by the licensee.
The licensee may vary or withdraw the undertaking at any time, but only with the consent of the Secretary.

section.heading: Enforcing undertakings

content.p: If the Secretary considers that a licensee who gave an undertaking under section 18QD has breached a term of the undertaking, the Secretary may apply to the Federal Court of Australia or the Federal Circuit and Family Court of Australia (Division 2) for an order under subsection (2).
If the court is satisfied that the licensee has breached a term of the undertaking, the court may make one or more of the following orders:
an order directing the licensee to comply with that term of the undertaking;

an order directing the licensee to pay to the Commonwealth an amount up to the amount of any financial benefit that the licensee has obtained directly or indirectly and that is reasonably attributable to the breach;
any order that the court considers appropriate directing the person to compensate any other person who has suffered loss or damage as a result of the breach;
any other order that the court considers appropriate.

section.heading: Secretary may publicise grounds on which disciplinary action taken, etc.

content.p: The Secretary may publicise, in any way he or she thinks appropriate, the grounds on which disciplinary action is taken against a licensee, and the disciplinary action taken.
This section does not:
limit the Secretary’s powers to publicise those details; or
prevent anyone else from publicising those details; or
affect any obligation (however imposed) on anyone to publicise those details.

division.heading: Appointment of utility meter verifiers on application

section.heading: Applying to be a utility meter verifier

content.p: A person may apply for appointment as a utility meter verifier.
An application must be:
made in the form approved by the Secretary; and
given to the Secretary.

section.heading: Appointment of utility meter verifiers

content.p: The Secretary may, in writing, appoint a person who has applied under section 18R to be a utility meter verifier.
The appointment must specify the class or classes of utility meters that the utility meter verifier may verify under the appointment.

The Secretary must not specify a class of utility meter that the utility meter verifier may verify unless the Secretary is satisfied that the verifier, or an employee of the verifier, is competent to test that class of utility meter.
An appointment is subject to:
the conditions set out in paragraphs 18RB(a) to (g); and
any other conditions that the Secretary imposes.
The Secretary may impose a condition referred to in paragraph (3)(b) at the time of making the appointment or after the appointment is made. The Secretary may vary or revoke a condition at any time.
Except when acting under section 18RG (following a breach of conditions), the Secretary must not impose, vary or revoke a condition unless the utility meter verifier has first been consulted.

section.heading: Conditions on appointment of utility meter verifiers

content.p: The appointment of a person as a utility meter verifier under section 18RA is subject to the following conditions:
if the verifier is an individual—that the verifier must not personally verify a utility meter unless he or she is competent to test that class of utility meter;
that the verifier must not employ a person to verify a utility meter unless that person is competent to test that class utility meter;
if the verifier employs persons to verify utility meters—that the verifier provide a list to the Secretary of the employees who will verify utility meters;
that the verifier, and its employees (if any), comply with the requirements of this Act;
that the verifier, and its employees (if any), comply with the requirements of a trade measurement inspector made under this Act;
that the verifier maintain such reference standards of measurement as the Secretary specifies in writing;
that the verifier participate in such training in respect of the verification of utility meters as the Secretary requires in writing;
that the verifier report as required in writing by the Secretary concerning its role as a utility meter verifier.

section.heading: Secretary must allocate utility meter verifier’s mark

content.p: When the Secretary appoints a utility meter verifier under section 18RA, the Secretary must allocate the following utility meter verifier’s marks for use by the verifier, or its employees (if any), when verifying utility meters:
if the verifier will be personally undertaking the verification—a mark for use by the verifier; and
if the verifier will be employing persons to undertake the verification—a separate mark for use by each employee.

section.heading: NATA accredited verifiers

content.p: For the purposes of subsection 18RA(2A), and for the purposes of the conditions set out in paragraphs 18RB(a) and (aa), a person who is accredited by the National Association of Testing Authorities to test a class of utility meter is taken to be competent to test that class of utility meter.

division.heading: Disciplinary action against utility meter verifiers appointed on application

section.heading: Notice to utility meter verifier of intention to take disciplinary action

content.p: If the Secretary is of the opinion that there may be grounds for taking disciplinary action under section 18RG against a utility meter verifier appointed under section 18RA because it is in breach of a condition of its appointment, the Secretary must:
give the verifier written notice of the Secretary’s opinion specifying the reasons for the opinion; and
invite the verifier to make a written submission to the Secretary within 14 days.

section.heading: Secretary may seek further information

content.p: The Secretary may ask the utility meter verifier, in writing, to give to the Secretary, within the period specified in the request, information for the purpose of making a decision under section 18RG.

section.heading: Secretary must consider utility meter verifier’s submission and information in making a decision under section 18RG

content.p: In making a decision under section 18RG in respect of a utility meter verifier, the Secretary must have regard to the matters raised in the verifier’s submission (if any) and any information received by the Secretary under section 18RE.

section.heading: Taking of disciplinary action against a utility meter verifier

content.p: If the Secretary is satisfied that a utility meter verifier appointed under section 18RA has breached a condition of its appointment, the Secretary may decide:
to take any or all of the following actions in respect of the breach:
to reprimand the verifier;
to vary or revoke a condition of the verifier’s appointment or to impose a further condition on the verifier’s appointment;
to suspend the verifier’s appointment for up to 12 months; or
to revoke the verifier’s appointment.
The following actions take effect on a day specified in writing by the Secretary:
a variation or revocation of a condition of a utility meter verifier’s appointment;
the imposition of a further condition on a utility meter verifier’s appointment;
the revocation of a utility meter verifier’s appointment.
Written notice of a decision of the Secretary under this section must be given to the utility meter verifier concerned. The notice must also include reasons for the decision.

The day specified by the Secretary under subsection (2) must not be a day earlier than the seventh day after the day on which written notice of the Secretary’s decision under this section is given to the utility meter verifier.

division.heading: Appointing Commonwealth or State officials etc. as utility meter verifiers

section.heading: Appointment of Commonwealth or State officials etc. as utility meter verifiers

content.p: The Secretary may, in writing, appoint one or more of the following person to be utility meter verifiers:
an APS employee (whether or not in the Department);
a Commonwealth authority;
an employee (whether or not an APS employee) of a Commonwealth authority;
the holder of an office established by or under a law of the Commonwealth;
a body corporate established for a public purpose by or under a law of a State or Territory;
a State or Territory officer.
The Secretary may appoint a body or person mentioned in paragraph (1)(e) or (f) only if the State or Territory concerned agrees to the appointment.
The appointment must specify:
the class or classes of utility meters that the utility meter verifier may verify under the appointment; and
the period of the appointment.
An appointment is subject to conditions that the Secretary imposes.
The Secretary may impose a condition at the time of making the appointment or after the appointment is made.

section.heading: Secretary must allocate verification marks to utility meter verifiers appointed under section 18RH

content.p: When the Secretary appoints a utility meter verifier under section 18RH, the Secretary must allocate the following verification marks for use by the verifier, or its employees (if any), when verifying utility meters:
if the verifier will be personally undertaking the verification—a mark for use by the verifier; and
if the verifier will be employing persons to undertake the verification—a separate mark for use by each employee.

section.heading: Maintaining of standards of measurement etc. before regulations prescribing units take effect

content.p: Where regulations that prescribe units of measurement of physical quantities are made under section 7A, but the regulations are not, or part of the regulations is not, to take effect immediately upon the date of notification of the regulations in the Gazette:
standards of measurement of those physical quantities may be maintained under section 8;
the powers conferred by section 8A may be exercised; and
State primary standards of measurement, and reference standards of measurement, of those physical quantities may be verified, and certificates issued in respect of the verification;
at any time after the date of notification of the regulations in the Gazette, as if the whole of the regulations had taken effect on that date.

section.heading: Patterns of instruments

content.p: The regulations may make provision for or in relation to:
the examination of patterns of measuring instruments;
the approval and verification of patterns of measuring instruments as patterns of measuring instruments suitable for:
use for trade; and
any other legal purpose;
the issuing of certificates in respect of the approval and verification of patterns of measuring instruments; and
the reception in evidence of a document purporting to be such a certificate and the admission as prima facie evidence of the matters stated in the document.
The regulations made under subsection (1) may provide that:
examinations may be carried out;
approvals may be given; and
certificates may be issued;
by the Chief Metrologist, a delegate of the Chief Metrologist or another person on behalf of the Chief Metrologist.

Without limiting the matters that may be provided for in regulations made for the purposes of subsection (1), the regulations may provide that the granting of approval of a pattern of a measuring instrument as a pattern suitable for use for trade may be made subject to the retention of the measuring instrument or a part of the measuring instrument by the Chief Metrologist.
Before the Governor-General makes a regulation for the purposes of subsection (1), the Minister must also either:

be satisfied that the regulation is not inconsistent with a specification published by the International Organisation of Legal Metrology regarding the examination and approval of patterns of measuring instrument; or
if the regulation is inconsistent with a specification—be satisfied that:
the inconsistency is in the national interest; or
it is not practicable to comply with the specification because of particular circumstances applying in Australia.
The Chief Metrologist may charge the prescribed fee for:
the examination of patterns of measuring instruments under this section; and
the approval and verification of patterns of measuring instruments as patterns of measuring instruments under this section; and
the issuing of certificates in respect of the approval and verification of patterns of measuring instruments under this section.

section.heading: Tolerances

content.p: The regulations may provide that a certificate issued under paragraph 19A(1)(c) in respect of a pattern of a measuring instrument (original instrument) must specify:
the limits of error that may be tolerated in a measuring instrument of the same kind as the original instrument when the instrument is tested for the purposes of this Act; and
the procedures to be followed to ascertain whether the instrument operates within those limits of error.

section.heading: Measuring instrument—accordance with pattern

content.p: The regulations may provide for:
the requirements that are to be satisfied before a measuring instrument with an approved pattern is taken, for the purposes of this Act, to be in accordance with the pattern; and
the procedures to be followed to ascertain whether measuring instruments with an approved pattern are in accordance with the pattern.
The regulations may provide that the procedures referred to in paragraph (1)(b) may be carried out:
by the Chief Metrologist; or
by a delegate of the Chief Metrologist; or
by another person on behalf of the Chief Metrologist.
Any regulations made under this section must provide adequate safeguards for the rights of persons affected.

section.heading: Offences

content.p: A person shall not falsely represent:
that a pattern of a measuring instrument is in accordance with a pattern approved under the regulations; or
that a measuring instrument is in accordance with a pattern so approved.
Penalty: 60 penalty units.

section.heading: Offences committed by employees—liability of employee

content.p: A person is not criminally responsible for an offence against a provision of Part IV, V, VI or VII if:
a physical element of the offence is committed by the person as an employee; and
the person was acting within the actual or apparent scope of his or her employment.

section.heading: Offences committed by employees—liability of employer

content.p: (1) If a physical element of an offence against a provision of Part IV, V, VI or VII is committed by an employee of a person (the employer) other than a body corporate acting within the actual or apparent scope of his or her employment, the physical element must also be attributed to the employer.

If intention, knowledge or recklessness is a fault element in relation to a physical element of the offence, that fault element must be attributed to the employer if the employer expressly, tacitly or impliedly authorised or permitted the commission of the offence.

section.heading: Offences committed by agents—liability of agent

content.p: A person is not criminally responsible for an offence against a provision of Part IV, V, VI or VII if:
a physical element of the offence is committed by the person as an agent of another person; and
the person was acting within the actual or apparent scope of his or her authority.

section.heading: Offences committed by agents—liability of principal

content.p: (1) If a physical element of an offence against a provision of Part IV, V, VI or VII is committed by an agent of a person (the principal) other than a body corporate acting within the actual or apparent scope of his or her authority, the physical element must also be attributed to the principal.

If intention, knowledge or recklessness is a fault element in relation to a physical element of the offence, that fault element must be attributed to the principal if the principal expressly, tacitly or impliedly authorised or permitted the commission of the offence.

section.heading: Protected information

content.p: This section applies to a person:
who is or has been a trade measurement inspector; or
who is or has been employed or engaged by the Department; or
who is performing, or has performed, functions or duties under this Act.
A person to whom this section applies commits an offence if:
the person obtains protected information; and
the person does any of the following:
copies, or makes a record of, the protected information;
uses the protected information;
discloses the protected information to any person.
Penalty: Imprisonment for 2 years.
Subsection (2) does not apply if:
the person copies, records, uses or discloses the protected information for the purposes of performing functions or exercising powers under this Act; or
the person obtains the protected information for any other lawful purpose; or
the person obtains consent from the person to whom the protected information relates for the copying, recording, use or disclosure of the protected information; or

the person believes, on reasonable grounds, that the copying, recording, use or disclosure of the protected information is necessary for the purpose of preserving the safety of another person or other persons.
Note 1: A defendant bears an evidential burden in relation to a matter in subsection (3), see subsection 13.3(3) of the Criminal Code.
Note 2: The Privacy Act 1988 also imposes limitations on the use or disclosure of protected information if it is personal information for the purposes of that Act.
Except where it is necessary to do so for the purposes of giving effect to this Act, the person must not be required to:
produce to a court a document containing protected information; or
disclose protected information to a court.
In this section:
court includes any tribunal, authority or person having power to require the production of documents or the answering of questions.
personal information has the same meaning as in the Privacy Act 1988.
protected information means information acquired under or for the purposes of this Act that is:
personal information; or
information that relates to the personal affairs or business affairs of a person.

section.heading: Review by Administrative Review Tribunal of decisions under this Act

content.p: An application may be made to the Administrative Review Tribunal for the review of each of the following decisions:
a decision under section 18JX to refuse to issue a permit;
a decision under section 18NB to refuse an application by a person to be a servicing licensee;
a decision under section 18NG to impose a condition on a servicing licence;
a decision under subsection 18NG(3) to amend a condition of a servicing licence;
a decision under section 18NI to refuse an application to amend a condition of a servicing licence;
a decision under section 18NJ to refuse an application to amend a servicing licence because of a change in the partnership holding the licence;
a decision under section 18NL to refuse to renew a servicing licence;
a decision under section 18NN to make an order in respect of a person;
a decision under section 18PB to refuse an application by a person to be a public weighbridge licensee;
a decision under section 18PG to impose a condition on a public weighbridge licence;
a decision under subsection 18PG(3) to amend a condition of a public weighbridge licence;
a decision under section 18PI to refuse an application to amend a condition of a public weighbridge licence;
a decision under section 18PJ to refuse an application to amend a public weighbridge licence because of a change in the partnership holding the licence;
a decision under section 18PM to refuse to renew a public weighbridge licence;
a decision under section 18PP to revoke a public weighbridge licence;
a decision under section 18PQ, 18PR or 18PS to make an order in respect of a person;
a decision under section 18QC to take disciplinary action against a servicing licensee or a public weighbridge licensee;
a decision under section 18RA to refuse an application by a person to be a utility meter verifier;
a decision under paragraph 18RA(3)(b) to impose a condition on a utility meter verifier’s appointment;
a decision under subsection 18RA(4) to vary or revoke a condition on a utility meter verifier’s appointment;
a decision under section 18RG to take disciplinary action against a utility meter verifier.

section.heading: Jurisdiction of the Federal Court of Australia and the Federal Circuit and Family Court of Australia (Division 2)

content.p: Jurisdiction is conferred on the Federal Court of Australia and the Federal Circuit and Family Court of Australia (Division 2) in respect of matters arising under the following provisions:
section 18LN;
section 18LO;
in relation to the Federal Court of Australian only—section 18MR;
section 18QE.

section.heading: Fees recoverable as a debt due to the Commonwealth

content.p: A fee payable under this Act may be recovered in a court of competent jurisdiction as a debt due to the Commonwealth.

section.heading: Rights may be amended, suspended or cancelled etc.

content.p: A right granted under this Act is granted on the basis that:
where the right is a servicing licence:
it may be amended under section 18NG or 18NI or paragraph 18QC(1)(b); and
it may be suspended or cancelled under paragraph 18QC(1)(c) or (e); and
where the right is a public weighbridge licence:
it may be amended under section 18PG or 18PI or paragraph 18QC(1)(b); and
it may be suspended or cancelled under paragraph 18QC(1)(c) or (e); and
where the right is a permit granted under section 18JX—it may be amended or cancelled under subsection 18JX(8); and
where the right is in relation to an appointment as a utility meter verifier:
it may be amended under section 18RA or 18RG; and
it may be suspended or revoked under section 18RG;
in the case of any right—it may be cancelled, revoked, terminated or amended by or under subsequent legislation; and
no compensation is payable if the right is cancelled, revoked, terminated or amended as mentioned in any of the above paragraphs.
(2) For the purposes of this section, right includes anything that is property within the meaning of paragraph 51(xxxi) of the Constitution.

section.heading: Compensation for acquisition of property

content.p: If the operation of this Act would result in an acquisition of property from a person otherwise than on just terms, the Commonwealth is liable to pay a reasonable amount of compensation to the person.

If the Commonwealth and the person do not agree on the amount of the compensation, the person may institute proceedings in a court of competent jurisdiction for the recovery from the Commonwealth of such reasonable amount of compensation as the court determines.
In this section:
acquisition of property has the same meaning as in paragraph 51(xxxi) of the Constitution.
just terms has the same meaning as in paragraph 51(xxxi) of the Constitution.

section.heading: Evidentiary matters—signature of Secretary or trade measurement inspector

content.p: A document purporting to be signed by the Secretary or a trade measurement inspector is taken to be signed by that person unless the contrary is established.

section.heading: Chief Metrologist may determine matters

content.p: The Chief Metrologist may determine, in writing:
AQS sampling procedures for the purposes of Subdivision 3-C of Division 3 of Part VI; and
AQS test procedures for the purposes of Subdivision 3-C of Division 3 of Part VI; and
national group test procedures for the purposes of Subdivision 4-B of Division 4 of Part VI; and
national sampling procedures for the purposes of Subdivision 4-B of Division 4 of Part VI; and
national single article test procedures for the purposes of Subdivision 4-B of Division 4 of Part VI.
A determination under subsection (1) is not a legislative instrument.

section.heading: Regulations

content.p: The Governor-General may make regulations, not inconsistent with this Act, prescribing all matters which are required or permitted to be prescribed, or which are necessary or convenient to be prescribed for carrying out or giving effect to this Act, and in particular:
providing for the verification of standards of measurement; and

providing for or in relation to the issuing of certificates in respect of the verification of standards of measurement, for the reception in evidence of a document purporting to be such a certificate and for such a certificate to be prima facie evidence of the matters stated in it; and
providing for the provision, maintenance, custody and care of standards of measurement; and

providing that a reference standard of measurement of a particular denomination that was found, upon verification, not to be greater or less than that denomination by an amount exceeding an amount specified in the regulations is, unless otherwise stated in the certificate issued in respect of the verification of the standard, to be deemed to be of a value equal to its denomination; and
providing for the certification of reference materials; and
providing for the certification of measuring instruments; and

providing for or in relation to the issuing of certificates in respect of the certification of reference materials or measuring instruments, for the reception in evidence of a document purporting to be such a certificate and for such a certificate to be prima facie evidence of the matters stated in it; and

providing for or in relation to the issuing of certificates in respect of measurements of an article, for reception in evidence of a document purporting to be such a certificate and for such a certificate to be prima facie evidence of the matters stated in it; and
prescribing classes of utility meters that are exempt utility meters; and
providing for sampling plans for utility meter verification; and
providing for the positioning of, and access to, utility meters in order to facilitate their use for trade and their verification; and

providing for the Commonwealth to audit the verification of utility meters used for trade undertaken by utility meter verifiers and the provision of labour, facilities and equipment for those purposes; and
providing for the verification of measuring instruments used for trade; and
providing for the positioning of, and access to, measuring instruments in order to facilitate their use by a person for trade, their examination by a verifier and their verification; and
providing for the sealing of a measuring instrument that has been verified; and
providing for quality assurance for measuring instruments used by persons for trade, and the provision of labour, facilities and equipment for that purpose; and
providing for matters applicable to weighbridges, whether or not public weighbridges, including their installation, functioning, operation, examination, testing, suitability and use; and
providing for the functions of operators of public weighbridges; and
regulating the advertising of articles (including articles packed in advance ready for sale) in so far as the advertising relates to measurement; and
providing for the keeping of records relating to measuring instruments and articles or utilities sold, or to be sold, by measurement; and
prescribing a fee for applications; and
prescribing a fee for activities undertaken in respect of:
the examination and certification of patterns of measuring instruments; and
the verification of measuring instruments used for trade; and
the issue of a certificate in relation to the verification of a measuring instrument used for trade; and
the issue of a permit for a packed article under Division 5 of Part VI; and
providing for the time for payment of a fee; and
(n) prescribing appropriate limits of error for a measuring instrument for the purposes of the definition of measuring instrument gives an inaccurate measurement; and
prescribing the re-verification period for a class of measuring instrument; and
prescribing AQS marks; and
prescribing AQS thresholds for the purposes of Subdivision 3-C of Division 3 of Part VI; and
prescribing the circumstances in which a group of packages is taken to have failed testing in accordance with AQS test procedures; and
prescribing national test thresholds for the purposes of Subdivision 4-B of Division 4 of Part VI; and
prescribing the circumstances in which a group of packages is taken to have failed testing in accordance with national group test procedures; and

The legislation history in endnote 3 provides information about each law that has amended (or will amend) the compiled law. The information includes commencement details for amending laws and details of any application, saving or transitional provisions that are not included in this compilation.

The amendment history in endnote 4 provides information about amendments at the provision (generally section or equivalent) level. It also includes information about any provision of the compiled law that has been repealed in accordance with a provision of the law.

The Legislation Act 2003 authorises First Parliamentary Counsel to make editorial and presentational changes to a compiled law in preparing a compilation of the law for registration. The changes must not change the effect of the law. Editorial changes take effect from the compilation registration date.

If the compilation includes editorial changes, the endnotes include a brief outline of the changes in general terms. Full details of any changes can be obtained from the Office of Parliamentary Counsel.

A misdescribed amendment is an amendment that does not accurately describe how an amendment is to be made. If, despite the misdescription, the amendment can be given effect as intended, then the misdescribed amendment can be incorporated through an editorial change made under section 15V of the Legislation Act 2003.
If a misdescribed amendment cannot be given effect as intended, the amendment is not incorporated and “(md not incorp)” is added to the amendment history.
